name: LA TAKIZA
notes: Router flagged latakiza.com's Clover storefront (taqueria-la-takiza-vista-vista.cloveronline.com) as screened-out: 93% of 41 prices land on a round number after dividing by 1.04, i.e. a 4% online-ordering fee baked into that channel. That storefront was NOT used. Instead, the restaurant's own website (a SpotHopper-built site, static.spotapps.co/tmt.spotapps.co) carries a separate, non-ordering 'Our Menu' / 'Our Drinks' page presenting prices directly in plain HTML (food-item-holder blocks, not a shopping cart) - confirmed as the Vista location via the page's own config.spot_id=31141, matching the 'vista-vista' slug in the Clover URL the router already resolved for this address. Ran the same markup test on these 21 food + 7 drink prices independently: no divisor (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/0.96) produces a round-number cluster; cents scatter across .89/.49/.95/.99/.50/.75/.90/.25/.00 with no pattern, consistent with genuine POS pricing rather than a marked-up feed. Two items (Tacos Harina, and the Mulitas/Burrito entries) print two prices on the same line for a base filling vs. premium filling (Lengua/Buche/Tripa/Fish) - both prices are printed plainly on the page, so both are recorded as separate rows rather than picking one. Menudo and Cebolla print small/large tiers, both recorded. A 'Specials' page for this location was checked and is empty ('We are updating our specials'). None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated.

name: Brick & Bell Cafe - La Jolla Shores
notes: Router's domain (brickandbellcafelajollashores.site) is dead - confirmed via nslookup (resolves to 162.255.119.99) but curl gets a connection timeout on port 443 (retried once with -v: TCP connect times out, no TLS handshake even attempted), so the domain itself has no live web server. The restaurant's real, current domain is brickandbell.com (a 4-location chain: Village, Shores, Ximed, Plus); its /location/shores page matches the work-list address exactly (2216 Avenida De La Playa, La Jolla). The page embeds ALL FOUR locations' prices in one HTML document as CSS-classed <li> fields (e.g. class="field-entry price-small-12oz-shores shores"), so every price was filtered strictly to the 'shores'-tagged entries only - a naive tag-strip of this page would silently interleave Village/Ximed/Plus prices with Shores prices for the same item name, which was caught and avoided. 116 distinct menu items yielding 194 priced rows once size/half-full tiers are split into separate rows (e.g. 'BLT (Half)' / 'BLT (Full)', 'Blueberry (Mini)' / 'Blueberry (Big)') across 17 sections: Hot Drinks, Iced Drinks, Espresso, Smoothies, Loose Leaf Teas, Fresh Juices, Fresh Brewed Iced Teas, Frappuccinos, Proteins Shake, Extras, Soft Drinks, Breakfast, Sandwich, Scones, Pastries & Desserts, Salads, Kid Options, Soup. Prices are POS-style odd-cent figures ($8.55, $7.94, $2.32, $2.78, $1.39) with no consistent divisor found under the markup test - not a delivery/ordering channel, this is the restaurant's own descriptive menu page. Modifier add-on prices mentioned in item descriptions (e.g. 'add: bacon +$1.50') were kept as description text, not split into separate dishes. None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated.

name: Saiko Sushi
notes: Router said no-platform; the own site (saikosushisd.com) is a single WordPress page with no HTML menu text, but it embeds two full-resolution photographed pages of the restaurant's own printed menu, filename-dated 2026/04 ('Saiko 2026 Menu'), read directly with the Read tool - a front page (food) and back page (sake/wine/beer/soda). Address on page (116 Orange Ave, Coronado, CA 92118) matches the work list exactly. Nigiri and Sashimi are each printed as one category price ($8 and $20 respectively) applying to every fish type listed under that heading, not a per-type price - recorded each type at that shared price, not merged into one row, since each is a distinct orderable dish. Three items (Farmer's Market Vegetables, Kama & Kabuto, Chef's Selection Market Fish) are marked 'MP' with no printed number and were dropped per the no-price rule. Happy Hour items are genuine daypart price variants of the same dishes sold at regular prices and were kept as separate rows, each labeled '(Happy Hour)'. Draft beer (Sapporo, Saiko Lager, Craft Breweries, both in Happy Hour and the regular Draft Beer section) and two bottled beers (Asahi, Kirin) print two numbers with no unit label (e.g. '8/28', '7|11') - labeled Glass/Pitcher and Bottle/Large Bottle respectively as a judgement call following standard restaurant menu convention, since the menu itself does not print the unit; flagged here rather than guessed silently. Wine is printed as Glass|Bottle (no legend, same judgement-call convention) except Conquilla Cava, explicitly labeled '(Half Bottle)' on the menu. Sake is printed as three tiers (Glass|Carafe|Bottle) with an explicit on-page legend ('Glass 4.5oz | Carafe 9oz | Bottle 24oz'), so those three labels are directly from the menu, not inferred. 171 dishes total. None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated beyond the disclosed unit-label judgement calls.

name: Mariscos El Titanic
notes:
Router said no-platform on the .shop domain. Verified this is not a directory-farm domain per the playbook's warning about cheap-TLD name-matched domains: curl -sIL shows no redirect at all (stays on mariscoseltitanic.shop, HTTP 200), and the /menu page carries a genuine, internally-consistent 116-item priced menu (structured

/ pairs inside per-section
blocks) at the exact work-list address (3600 Fairmount Ave, San Diego, CA 92105), matching the cuisine (Mexican mariscos/seafood - botanas, cocteles, tostadas de mariscos, camarones, pescado entero, tacos/burritos de mariscos). Corrected a section-attribution bug while extracting: the page alternates image-left/image-right layout rows, so in roughly half the rows the

section header appears in the HTML AFTER its item block rather than before - naive linear header-tracking misattributed ~40 items to the wrong section (e.g. all of 'Camarones' landing under 'Tostadas'); fixed by parsing each
wrapper as one unit (header + its own items together) rather than assuming header-then-items order. 19 named items across the page have a literal empty (six specialty micheladas/cocteles - Viagra, Masoquista, Matapasion, Dormilona, Torturadora, Locochona - plus a handful of others including the component list for the $78 'Fuente De Mariscos' seafood platter) and were dropped per the no-price rule rather than guessed. None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated.
